Vision.heroTitle: Our vision for human wellbeing and AI
Vision.heroSub: Human experience in an age of machine intelligence — and how mindfulness, compassion, and the Middle Way can help shape it.
Vision.carbonLead: The relationship between human minds and artificial intelligence is a defining question for our future.
Vision.carbonP1: AI systems process information at extraordinary speed. Human experience encompasses embodied awareness, vulnerability, empathy, and moral responsibility. As these systems become more influential, we must consider both the goals they pursue and the human behaviours reflected in their training data.
Vision.carbonP2: The concern is not limited to deliberately harmful machines. Human-generated data can also contain conflict, polarisation, and reactive behaviour. Our proposal asks how a greater emphasis on calm attention and compassion might contribute to technology designed around human wellbeing.
Vision.middleDesc: The initiative draws on the Buddhist principle of the Middle Way. Applied to technology, it encourages progress guided by human wellbeing and ethical reflection — avoiding both technological development that disregards its human consequences, and a wholesale rejection of scientific progress.

Vision.stupaLead: A carefully governed dataset associated with mindfulness, compassion, and flow states.
Vision.stupaP1: Named for the stupa — a Buddhist monument that embodies a repository of contemplative experience — its purpose is to support research on the relationship between experience, physiology, and the design of supportive AI. EEG and other physiological measures would complement participants' own accounts, as research observations rather than a “gold standard” of consciousness.
Vision.stupaP2: Whether this work can contribute to safer, more beneficial AI is a question to investigate — not an established outcome.
Vision.aspirationDesc: Technology helps people understand and develop their inner lives; human wisdom helps guide technology.
Vision.ctaDesc: Explore how attention, compassion, and resilience can inform a future shaped by AI.

Science.heroTitle: The science of a shared breath
Science.heroSub: Turning the vision into a useful experience requires collaboration across hardware, software, and neuroscience — through the proposed Multimodal Mindfulness Index.
Science.mmiLead: The MMI would bring together EEG, cardiac, and breathing measurements to provide understandable feedback during practice.
Science.mmiP: The approach draws on work at HKU's Centre of Buddhist Studies and the Centre on Behavioral Health. The intended research programme examines how physiological measures relate to attention, relaxation, and emotional regulation. The MMI would require validation before it could support clinical claims or meaningful comparisons between people.

measures.title: Wavelet Entropy
measures.desc: Signal organisation during mindfulness, informing a proposed Clarity Score.

measures.title: Alpha & Theta
measures.desc: 8–12 Hz and 4–7 Hz activity, linked to relaxed alertness.

measures.title: Brain–Heart Coordination
measures.desc: EEG with heart rate variability — harmony between mind and body.

measures.title: Mindfulness Score
measures.desc: A 0–100 feedback tool — a guide to practice, not a judgement.

Science.privacyLead: The proposed architecture prioritises processing on the device or phone where feasible.
Science.privacyP: The shared community visualisation would use aggregated, de-identified features rather than individuals' raw neural signals. Optional research data collection — and any later use for AI training — would require a separate, clearly explained consent process and appropriate governance.
privacyChecklist: No neural data required for basic practice
Separate, clearly explained consent for research
Feedback is supportive, never a grade of worth

Research.joinTitle: Bring a study, a clinic, or a cohort
Research.joinLead: The research is only as good as the people in it. We are looking for partners who can host a study, share anonymised data, or help fund measurement rather than marketing.
joinPoints: Researchers: joint studies, shared protocols, open data where consent allows
Clinicians and teachers: pilot the practices with the people you already serve
Funders: measurement and validation first — the part that rarely gets funded
Participants: join a study, or practise with the community in the meantime

Practice.heroSub: Ocean-guided breathing, meditation, and compassion — accessible to everyone, free at the core.
Practice.oceanLead: Ocean sounds provide a central sensory language for the platform — a simple cue that needs no charts or lengthy instructions.
Practice.oceanP: The sound design explores gentle cycles of approximately 10–12 seconds — about six breaths a minute (0.1 Hz), a rhythm linked to resonance in paced breathing. A generative audio engine can adapt to your own rhythm and gently invite a slower, more comfortable pace.
Practice.practicesDesc: Presented in accessible, non-sectarian language — sometimes described as “fitness for the mind”.
Practice.universalDesc: Accessible practice for individuals and communities.

Community.heroTitle: A global community of shared practice
Community.heroSub: Connecting individual practice with a shared global rhythm — a rolling “Mindfulness Hour” that follows the evening around the world.
Community.relayLead: The proposed model organises communities into 12 regional time-zone groups across the 24-hour day, using two-hour planning bands.
Community.relayP: Each community holds a local Mindfulness Hour from 10:00–11:00 pm — the core session runs 10:00–10:30 pm, followed by 30 minutes of optional reflection, a gentle transition from daily activity to rest.
Community.citiesTitle: Following the evening around the globe
Community.liveTitle: Where the Mindfulness Hour is unfolding
Community.liveDesc: Computed live from each city's local time. Mindfulness Hour runs 10:00–11:00 pm local.
Community.hubLead: A live digital space for shared practice, visualised as a three-dimensional globe of participating communities.
Community.hubP: Where sufficient consented data are available, aggregated feedback from the Professional tier could influence the display — an active region might become brighter, or a virtual ocean calmer. These effects represent participation and selected data, not a physical global “energy field”.
Community.ctaDesc: Shared attention and intention can help people feel less isolated and more connected — across cultures and without a common language.

Support.heroSub: Help widen access to contemplative practice — and grow the Spiritual Oasis programme for communities facing barriers to participation.
Support.oasisLead: A community's wellbeing includes those with the fewest resources.
Support.oasisP: We propose working with local charities and community organisations in underserved regions — including parts of Africa and the wider Global South — and with communities affected by displacement, incarceration, or social exclusion. Practical support should respond to people's circumstances and be developed with organisations that understand their languages, cultures, and local needs.
